title: Docker Monitoring
subtitle: Logs, metrics, events and health
description: A running container is not the same as a healthy service. Learn the signals Docker exposes and how to turn them into a monitoring stack you can trust.
outcomes: Use stats, events and health checks effectively
Build a cAdvisor + Prometheus + Grafana stack

lessons.title: Stats and events
lessons.summary: The built-in telemetry: resource usage snapshots and the Docker event stream.
objectives: Read docker stats and docker events
Filter events by type and object
Know the limits of built-in metrics

sections.title: Events tell the story
sections.body:
`docker events` streams daemon-level events: container start/die/oom, image pull, network connect, volume mount. Filter with `--filter type=container --filter event=die` or by label. Events are essential for correlating a failure with a deployment or OOM kill.

Stats are point-in-time resource samples. Neither is a long-term metrics store; export to Prometheus or your platform if you need retention and alerting.

sections.code:
docker events --filter type=container --filter event=die --format '{{json .}}'
docker events --since 1h --until now --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=acme
docker stats --no-stream
docker inspect --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}} {{.State.ExitCode}}' api

sections.title: Event retention is short
sections.body: The daemon keeps only recent events. If you need history, ship them to a log pipeline or use Prometheus-style metrics.

lessons.title: Logging drivers and rotation
lessons.summary: Where stdout goes, how to rotate it, and why JSON files fill disks.

sections.title: stdout is the contract
sections.body:
Applications should log to stdout/stderr. The daemon captures those streams with a logging driver. The default `json-file` writes files under `/var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/`; without rotation they can fill the disk.

`local` is a better default for many installations. `journald`, `syslog`, `fluentd`, `gelf` and cloud drivers ship logs elsewhere. Driver support differs by platform.

sections.code:
docker run -d --name api \
  --log-driver json-file \
  --log-opt max-size=10m \
  --log-opt max-file=3 \
  acme/api:1.4

docker inspect api --format '{{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}'
docker logs --since 15m --tail 200 api

# Daemon-wide default in /etc/docker/daemon.json
# { "log-driver": "local", "log-opts": { "max-size": "10m" } }
sections.note: Changing the daemon default does not rewrite existing containers; recreate them.

sections.title: docker logs only works with local drivers
sections.body: If you ship logs with a remote driver, `docker logs` may return nothing. Query the central system instead.

lessons.title: Health checks that mean something
lessons.summary: A port check is not a health check. Design probes that test the service contract.
objectives: Tune interval, timeout, retries and start period
Avoid health checks that damage the service

sections.title: What should be checked
sections.body: A good health check exercises the dependency path that matters: database connectivity, cache availability, or a `/health/ready` endpoint that verifies downstreams. A shallow TCP check only proves the process is listening. A deep check on every probe can overload dependencies — separate liveness (is the process alive?) from readiness (can it serve traffic?).

sections.note: The command must exit 0 for healthy and non-zero for unhealthy. Output is stored in the health log.

sections.code:
docker inspect --format '{{json .State.Health}}' api
docker ps --filter health=unhealthy

sections.title: Start period prevents restart storms
sections.body: Give slow starters time. Without start_period, a legitimate 40-second boot can be marked unhealthy and restarted repeatedly.

lessons.title: A cAdvisor + Prometheus + Grafana stack
lessons.summary: A practical Compose stack for container metrics, with the security caveats called out.
objectives: Deploy cAdvisor, Prometheus and Grafana with Compose

sections.title: The standard open-source stack
sections.body: cAdvisor reads container cgroups and exposes Prometheus metrics. Prometheus scrapes and stores them. Grafana queries Prometheus and renders dashboards. All three run comfortably in Compose on a single host. cAdvisor needs read access to the Docker socket and host cgroups; treat that access as sensitive and restrict the network.

sections.code:
services:
  cadvisor:
    image: gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor:v0.49.1
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8080:8080"]
    volumes:
      - /:/rootfs:ro
      - /var/run:/var/run:ro
      - /sys:/sys:ro
      - /var/lib/docker/:/var/lib/docker:ro
    devices:
      - /dev/kmsg
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.55.1
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:9090:9090"]
    networks: [monitoring]

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.3.0
    volumes:
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:3001:3000"]
    networks: [monitoring]

networks:
  monitoring:
volumes:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:
sections.note: This stack is for a trusted host. Do not publish cAdvisor or Prometheus publicly.

sections.code:
# prometheus.yml
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: cadvisor
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["cadvisor:8080"]
  - job_name: docker
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["host.docker.internal:9323"]
sections.note: The Docker daemon can expose metrics on :9323 when configured with metrics-addr.

sections.title: Mounting the Docker socket is a privilege
sections.body: cAdvisor and many exporters mount it read-only, but the socket is still powerful. Isolate the monitoring network and run the stack on a dedicated host or with a restricted socket proxy.
